      price-sensitive SMB accounts

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most

  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the

answer.rationale: The two live symptoms (onboarding completion -4% QoQ, activation -6% QoQ) point at a funnel/time-to-value problem, not a price problem. Two mutually reinforcing inherited records (memory_86 on shortening onboarding, memory_31 on cutting signup fields) both indicate that friction reduction lifts activation and early adoption in exactly the self-serve/SMB segment now under stress, and those gains accrue to accounts that arrived for product reasons, so they are more likely to convert into durable qualified revenue. I am verifying memory_86 because it is the direct basis for my chosen action and I want the original effect size, segment definition, and whether the lift persisted past week one or merely pulled completion forward. I am verifying memory_73 because it is the memory most likely to misdirect me right now: the competitor's entry pricing makes deep discounting feel like the obvious counter, and memory_73 is the most numerically confident record in the set (+31% trials, +18% quarterly revenue, 12 full weeks). That confidence is exactly why it deserves scrutiny. The stated outcomes are all top-of-funnel and single-quarter; the record says nothing about retention, expansion, renewal, or margin per acquired account, and discount-acquired price-sensitive small accounts are the cohort most prone to churning or repricing when the promotion lapses. A revenue number measured inside the discount window can look like growth while actually degrading downstream account value, and matching a competitor on price also risks resetting willingness-to-pay in the segment. So the +18% is not yet evidence of sustainable qualified revenue, and I want the source record to see what was and was not measured before I let it override the funnel diagnosis. Memory_57 (referrals) is about established customers, not the ailing self-serve top of funnel; memory_44 (enterprise sales-assist) addresses a different segment than the one that is bleeding. If verification shows memory_86's lift was thin, short-lived, or drawn from a non-comparable population, I will fall back to activation_messaging (memory_91), which targets the same week-one activation gap. If memory_73 unexpectedly turns out to include clean retention and post-promotion cohort data, I would reconsider promotional pricing as a guarded test only. Running as a standard experiment with holdout, and instrumenting not just completion and activation but 30/90-day retention and expansion, so this decision leaves behind a record that distinguishes real durable lift from a pulled-forward number.
